state.purpose: Advise a finite parser consolidation proposal for a public open-source project; no implementation or speedup is presumed.
facts: DESIGN requires one bounded ICU profile: named arguments, number/integer, date/time, nested plural/selectordinal/select with other, exact numeric cases, apostrophe-friendly quoting, no offsets/custom styles/rich handlers. It defines nearest plural pound but not pound outside plural.

Values has a public TS parser/AST, exact bigint selectors, unsigned decimal selector lexemes, normalized duplicates, finite CLDR categories and argument depth32. Values accepts pound outside plural as literal. UI has a private parser, broader keys and signed exact selectors, no explicit depth cap, weaker quoting/category checks and different syntax errors with UTF16 offsets.

UI already imports/depends on Values. UI and Values renderers have different scalar admission, decimal scale and localized digit behavior; replacing the renderer would change unrelated behavior. UI resolves locale and converts all supplied operands before parsing; Values rendering parses first. Locale, Intl, typed binding and host errors should remain with their existing adapters.

Compiler has a Rust parser mixing grammar/type checks and a separate permissive placeholder scanner. They disagree on friendly apostrophes, whitespace and branch scans. Typed anonymous descriptors now reuse the checker; named coverage diagnostics remain separate. Number style-before-type and date/time type-before-style order are observable.

Compiler already depends on the private values-semantics Rust crate. Values has explicit synchronous Wasm bootstrap and a JSON op transport but public parsing currently works without Wasm. JS string code units, public AST bigint fields and error offsets need preservation across a Rust boundary. No complete parser startup/copy/render workload benchmark has been established.
A prior pinned FormatJS0.3.1 comparison retained the bounded scanner because published exact selector and parse-time depth APIs failed the required profile. A new full ICU dependency is not assumed.

architecture.instructions: Which finite consolidation architecture best meets the public project contract at proportionate total maintenance and delivery cost? Compare all alternatives on the same observable behavior; do not infer unmeasured performance.

criteria.aligned_independent: Keep the three parser implementations, resolve the grammar contract and correct each owner using the same finite cases. Lowest integration change, but retains duplication and drift risk.
criteria.ts_first_shared_contract: Share the Values TS parser with UI, consolidate compiler grammar and usage into one Rust implementation using the same contract/cases, preserve adapters, and defer a cross-language Wasm switch to a finite comparison. Removes UI/scanner duplication now; retains two grammar implementations.
criteria.rust_shared_execution: Propose one Values-owned Rust grammar core for native compiler plus Wasm-backed Values/UI execution, with existing public wrappers. Removes cross-language grammar duplication, but requires startup, UTF16/string transport, error and installed-host work before adoption.

outside_plural_pound.instructions: Which outside-plural pound policy should the shared bounded grammar propose, considering runtime compatibility, compiler diagnostics and the stated specification gap?

criteria.literal: Specify unquoted pound outside any plural as literal, matching both runtime implementations; inside plural use nearest plural through nested select.
criteria.reject: Specify unquoted pound outside plural as an error, matching compiler; require runtime callers to quote it.
criteria.defer: Leave this lexical policy unresolved until a concrete additional use case is available, retaining the current mismatch meanwhile.
